# DeepSeek Web (DSH plugin)
**简体中文** · English

Two controls, one purpose: keep DeepSeek's web chat and your DSH Session in the
same window.

1. **Sidebar launcher** — beside **Settings** at the sidebar foot. Opens
`https://chat.deepseek.com/

` in the shipped right-Sidebar **Browser** tab,
next to the current Session. Clicking again focuses

the tab it already has.
2. **Composer bridge** — a small "pull" control in the composer tool row
(be

fore Send). One click reads the newest answer out of the DeepSeek panel
and inserts it into the curr

ent draft as one undoable edit, so you can hand
what the page produced straight to your agent.

The bridge prefers a live text selection inside the DeepSeek page; with nothing
selected it takes th
e last rendered answer block.

3. **Review tool** — the host half also registers `web_review`, so the agent can
send a prompt into

that same page and get the answer back as structured
findings. See Review bridge.
## Install

This is a **DSH Desktop bundle**, not an npm package. Distribution is the folder
itself.

1. Clone or download this repository somewhere permanent, e.g.
`C:\plugins\deepseek-web-panel`.
2. A

sk your DSH agent to install that directory as a bundle
(`plugin_manager` → `install_bundle` with th

e absolute path). The agent adds
the dependency as a `link:` and the bundle row to your profile, so

edits to
the folder stay live.
3. Restart DSH. The launcher appears at the sidebar foot, beside **Se

the folder stay live.
3. Restart DSH. The launcher appears at the sidebar foot, beside **Settings**.

Manual alternative: add `"@local/dsh-plugin-deepseek-web": "link:C:/path/to/deepseek-web-panel"`
to

your profile's `package.json`, list the package under `dsh.profile.bundles`,
and install; `cordis.pa
tch.yml` is the row this bundle inserts.
### Through a plugin market

This repository also publishes a **market index** (`market.json`, format 1). Add
one of these URLs u
nder **Settings → Plugins → Discover**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The jsDelivr mirrors are listed first because `raw.githubusercontent.com` is
unreachable from some n

etworks; the Host fetches the index itself, so pick one it
can reach.

The entry installs this repository as a commit-pinned Git package
(`git+https://github.com/LuoZIren/

dsh-deepseek-web.git#<commit>`), so an update
means a new commit and a new version in the index — an

d the installing machine
must be able to clone `github.com`. A market index is just a JSON file a re

ader
is configured with; there is no central registry to submit to.

Requirements: DSH Desktop (Electron) on Windows, macOS or Linux. The sign-in
patch targets the deskt

op `app.asar`; a DSH upgrade replaces that file, which the
status dot then reports.
## What it writes to your machine

- The status dot's repair path performs a **50-byte, equal-length rewrite** of a
single statement in

side the desktop `app.asar`, after saving
`app.asar.orig-bak`. It refuses to write when the archive'

s shape changed.
That rewrite is what keeps the DeepSeek sign-in across restarts; without it
every l

aunch asks you to sign in again.
- Nothing else is written outside your DSH profile. The review brid

ge types into
the DeepSeek page you already have open and reads its answer back.
## The status dot

A 6 px dot rides to the right of the launcher and reports whether the partition
patch is in place:
| Dot | Meaning |

| green | the archive carries the persistent statement |
| red | the statement is gone (an upgrade r

eplaced it) — **click the dot** to rewrite it |
| gray | not known yet: open the DeepSeek panel once

ick the dot** to rewrite it |
| gray | not known yet: open the DeepSeek panel once, or restart DSH |

Clicking a red dot asks the Host half to re-apply the patch; the tooltip then
says a restart is need

ed, because the running process keeps the partition it was
started with. A dot that stays red with "

the archive no longer matches this
patch" means a DSH build changed the statement itself — the plugi

n refuses to
write rather than risk the archive, and the patch text has to be re-derived.

The dot reads two sources, in order: the Host half's `GET /deepseek-web/patch`
(the archive itself),

and the live guest's `partition` attribute (what the
running process actually uses). The second one

is what makes the dot correct
before the Host half has been reloaded by a restart.
## Settings

Settings → **DeepSeek web chat** holds this plugin's preferences. They are
stored per browser profil

e (`dsh.deepseek-web.settings.v1`) and apply live — the
dot on the sidebar updates as you change the
m, without a reload.

| Status dot | Show the dot | Hides the dot entirely; the launcher stays. |
| | Dot size | 4, 6, or

## Why DeepSeek said "abnormal usage environment"
DeepSeek's own client ships a hard-coded check:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Either hit renders the `usageEnvUnsafeTitle` / `usageEnvUnsafeWarn` dialog
("使用环境异常 … 建议您使用我们的官方产品")

. In this guest `process` is not
exposed (`sandbox`, `contextIsolation`, no node), so the user agent

is the only
trigger. The plugin calls `webview.setUserAgent()` once per tab with the same
string mi

nus the `Electron/x.y.z` and application tokens — platform and Chromium
version untouched — and relo

ads, so the check no longer fires and the sign-in
request no longer advertises an embedded browser.

The dialog is dismissible and its "closed" flag is persisted storage, so once the
partition survives
restarts, a dismissed dialog stays dismissed too.
## Why it reuses the Browser tab

`chat.deepseek.com` answers with `content-security-policy: frame-ancestors
'none'`, so a plain `` pa

ge inside DSH cannot load it. The shipped
Browser tab type is the supported way around that: on Desk

top it embeds a real
Electron guest view (not a frame), which a site cannot refuse. The bridge then

reads that guest through `webview.executeJavaScript()`; the guest keeps
`sandbox`, `contextIsolation

`, and `nodeIntegration: false`, so nothing is
injected into the page and no Node access is granted.

In the browser build of DSH the same tab type falls back to an iframe and no
guest exists, so both c

ontrols report that embedded browsing is unavailable
instead of failing silently.
